subject: Combining censored survival observations with other data

messages.author: 9bcc3ae55bfcf64b
messages.subject: Combining censored survival observations with other data
parts:
Hi, 

I previously wrote a question predating this (here:  CDF as likelihood model and custom likelihood functions. (google.com)).

Using censored observations would be a viable method, but is it possible in INLA to combine the censored observations with ones using a regular likelihood? 

The examples showing survival models use inla.surv(time, cens) ~ ... specifying that the dependent variable is a survival object for all observations. It does not seem possible to connect the linear predictor to both types of observations using link functions. Is there any documentation detailing how to do this if it is possible? 

My aim is prediction of the latent field using the different observations. 

Best regards, 
Michael

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Combining censored survival observations with other data
parts:
sure. use `inla.surv' to define the survival part and then a regular
likelihood for the rest.


--
Håvard Rue
he...@r-inla.org

parts:
Thank you. 

I have run into some problems with constructing a very simple test case  (code appended) using a lognormal survival model. 
Running the model considering all observations as uncensored results in the same results as using a lognormal likelihood in a non survival model. However, censoring one of the observations causes the model to crash. Setting diagonal=something.large helps, but provides nonsensical results. While decreasing the value causes crashes before the model provides any results. 

Output from verbose=T are also appended. 

I am not sure how to proceed in debugging this. 

Best, 
Michael
